messages.author: d6ff3e4ce292e4dd
messages.subject: rOpenGov harmonized API calls?
parts:
Many have agreed it would be useful to have a harmonized API calls for related rOpenGov packages, for instance based on S4 classes. Although these are more laborious to implement, time is scarce, and coordination across package developers might be a challenge.

Anyway, some thoughts to start with (based on Joona's earlier suggestion).


1) Datamart

Datamart provides an example.
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/datamart/index.html
http://factbased.blogspot.fi/2012/06/a-wrapper-for-r-data-function.html

This would work as follows:

> library(helsinki)
> hel <- helsinki()
> queries(hel)
[1] "AddressList" "HSY" "DistrictBoundaries"
> addr <- query(hel, "AddressList")

A related (imaginary) package stockholm:

> library(stockholm)
> stk <- stockholm()
> queries(stk)
[1] "AddressList" "ZIPcodes"
> zip.codes <- query(stk, "ZIPcodes")

This demonstrates the advantages of a proper API. It is not clear whether Datamart itself is ready, so we should be cautious when considering their practices. Is it realistic to assume we have the resources to implement this sort of system? Perhaps we should just start with the option below, and make small-scale experimentation with datamart-type queries with specific packages (for instance between Finland + Sweden + Austria election data packages?) and see how it works there.

2) There is also a simple, alternative option without harmonized API that we have used so far in some packages:

GetSomeData("resource_name_or_url", local.dir = "~/tmp/", overwrite = FALSE)  

This would download the original data in the local folder. If the data has been retrieved already, the local copy will be used instead (helping with speed & documentation issues). This is much easier to implement, but more complicated for a regular user since the user needs to keep track on correct resource names etc. and these may differ between countries for instance. Unless we stay strict in harmonizing naming conventions across independent packages (a challenge in itself).

For each package it would also be good to have an additional function that lists all data resources that are available through that package. At the moment I am handling this by giving comprehensive list of examples in the Rmd vignette. But perhaps we will also need a separate function that provides a listing (?)

My suggestion is to start with option 2 to get things forward and packages ready for CRAN. We can then think Datamart-type solutions in a longer term with those who are interested in the implementation work and able to use their time for that.

Leo

messages.author: d6ff3e4ce292e4dd
messages.subject: Fwd: rOpenGov: rOpenGov harmonized API calls?
parts:
Hi Måns, I am replying to the ropengov discussion list where this thread started.

Your suggestion sounds worth trying. But I think the practical bottleneck is that designing and implementing S4 classes properly easily takes lots of time, and the advantages of such endeavour will need to be clear. At the moment most of our data access functions just download the full data matrix and store it in a local file (also good for reproducibility to keep the files) unless the user prevents this. And we do not really have more sophisticated access functions for the data (yet at least) since in many cases these can be handled with routine data.frame tools in R.

Personally I would be curious to even try a couple of different options in practice, if the time allows, and then see what works best in practice. If we will do something on EP election data sets, that could provide a test case. But time is scarce and that is something to acknowledge.

We had some discussion on this recently with Markus and Joona, they might have further comments.

Leo

Just a small question regarding part 2). Do you allways download your data to a given file (and the load the data)? In sweSCB we download Rdata into the current R session?
We use findData() in sweSCB to navigate the API and the GetData() to download.

Maybe an API harmonization should be focus on two steps:
1) Design the query (for example findData() ) and save this query as an S4 object and then use getData() on this S4 object. then it will be two distinct parts of the API call? Just a thought.

messages.author: ceb6545892b4dd19
messages.subject: Re: Fwd: rOpenGov: rOpenGov harmonized API calls?
parts:
Hi

I think I already wrote about this sometime ago, but here's to reiterate
few comments.

> Your suggestion sounds worth trying. But I think the practical
> bottleneck is that designing and implementing S4 classes properly easily
> takes lots of time, and the advantages of such endeavour will need to be
> clear.

To me, the advantage is simple enough: A common API. No matter what
package you'd be using at least the basic querying/fetching functions
(methods) would be the same. Having said that, Leo is absolutely correct
in that designing the data model / S4-classes would take more effort.
Since the common API would probably be restricted to
querying/fetching/metadata the design process probably wouldn't be too
overwhelming. BTW, as far the implementation goes S3 might be enough as
well. S3 is less formal than S4 and easier to implement.

> Personally I would be curious to even try a couple of different options
> in practice, if the time allows, and then see what works best in
> practice. If we will do something on EP election data sets, that could
> provide a test case. But time is scarce and that is something to
> acknowledge.

Couldn't agree more and in any case it's better to get something out
than nothing at all. I think experimenting with few options in the
beginning is a good strategy. I'll be trying something out with a S4
implementation once I get something going.

Cheers,

Joona
